why: A line parallel to the y-axis is vertical, so it has the form x = k; passing through (2, -3) forces k = 2. Option D (x = -3) is vertical but misses the point; A and B are horizontal (parallel to the x-axis), and A is the distractor that uses the point's y-coordinate.

For centre (a,b,c) the distances to the x-, y-, z-axes are sqrt(b^2+c^2), sqrt(a^2+c^2), sqrt(a^2+b^2); setting all three equal to r and adding gives a^2+b^2+c^2 = 3r^2/2, so a^2 = b^2 = c^2 = r^2/2 uniquely and each coordinate is +-r/sqrt(2). Sympy and an independent sign enumeration both return exactly 8 admissible centres, each verified at distance exactly r from all three axes.

The antiderivative of sec^2(2x)/2 is tan(2x)/4, giving tan(pi/4)/4 - tan(0)/4 = 1/4 exactly (confirmed symbolically). No two options are equivalent, and since 1/4 is itself printed, the 'None of these' option D does not apply.

floor(x^2) is 0 on [0,1), 1 on [1,sqrt2), 2 on [sqrt2,sqrt3) and 3 on [sqrt3,2), so the integral is (sqrt2-1) + 2(sqrt3-sqrt2) + 3(2-sqrt3) = 5 - sqrt2 - sqrt3. A 4-million-point midpoint Riemann sum agrees to 1.3e-7, and D is the only option matching exactly (A, B, C evaluate to 0.586, 3.414, 0.414).

|x|+|y|=1 bounds the square with vertices (1,0),(0,1),(-1,0),(0,-1); integrating the width 2(1-|x|) over [-1,1], the shoelace formula, and (1/2)*d1*d2 with both diagonals equal to 2 all give exactly 2. The side is sqrt(2), so the 2*sqrt(2) of option B is a side-length distractor, not the area.

value: y = e^(-2x)/4 + cx + d (the general solution, two arbitrary constants)
why: Integrating twice gives y = e^(-2x)/4 + cx + d, which sympy's dsolve reproduces exactly (C1 + C2*x + exp(-2x)/4). Option A also satisfies the ODE but carries zero arbitrary constants, so it is only a PARTICULAR solution - a proper subset of the solution set of a second-order equation - while C and D fail the ODE outright (y'' = 2c + e^(-2x) and 4e^(-4x)).

value: f'(0) does not exist: right-hand derivative +1, left-hand derivative -1
why: For x > 0, f(x) = e^x gives RHD = +1; for x < 0, f(x) = e^(-x) gives LHD = -1. Sympy's one-sided limits and 40-digit one-sided difference quotients both return +1 and -1, so the two-sided derivative fails to exist; a symmetric difference quotient would have falsely returned 0 and agreed with option C, which is why the one-sided test is the discriminating one.

A diagonal matrix has every off-diagonal entry zero; the only non-zero-by-construction off-diagonal entry here is the (3,2) entry b, so b = 0. Verified with sympy's is_diagonal: true only for b = 0 and false for 2, 1 and 3.

f'(a) = 4a - 3 = 0 at a = 3/4 with f''= 4 > 0, and f(3/4) = 71/8 exactly; the completed square 2(a - 3/4)^2 + 71/8 confirms it independently. The inequality f(a) <= 15/2 has no real solution, so the tempting option A is unattainable.

value: the monthly rainfall volumes over 24 consecutive months - a numerical series admitting aggregation and comparison
why: Statistical data must be quantitative facts collected so that they can be summarised, compared and analysed; options A, B and C are purely qualitative catalogues of names (no numerical variable and nothing to average or vary), whereas D is a numerical variable observed repeatedly over time.

a.b = 2 - 4 + 2 = 0 already, so only a.c = lambda - 1 + 2mu = 0 and b.c = 2lambda + 4 + mu = 0 remain; solving gives lambda = -3, mu = 2. Substituting each option confirms D is the only pair making both dot products vanish (A gives -5 and 5, B gives 3 and 3, C gives -2 and 8).

Pairing terms gives cos x + cos2x + cos3x + cos4x = 4 cos(5x/2) cos(x) cos(x/2) (identity verified symbolically and to 4.6e-41 at six awkward test points); the three factors contribute {(2k+1)pi/5} = 5 roots, {pi/2, 3pi/2} = 2 roots, and {pi}, which duplicates a root already in the first family, so 7 distinct values in [0,2pi). Each has residual exactly 0, and an independent dense sign-change scan found the same set - its apparent 8th hit is x = pi listed twice, because the function only touches zero there (f(pi +- 0.01) = -0.0005 on both sides) rather than crossing.

With x_i = i/(i+1) and f_i = i, each f_i/x_i = i(i+1)/i = i+1, so HM = (sum i) / (sum (i+1)) = [n(n+1)/2] / [n(n+3)/2] = (n+1)/(n+3). Sympy confirms the closed form and exact Fraction arithmetic reproduces it for n = 1..8 (1/2, 3/5, 2/3, 5/7, 3/4, ...), matching B every time while A and C go negative from n = 4. Since a printed option matches, 'None of these' does not apply.

Taking x - 3y + 4 = 0 as y on x and 2x - 7y + 8 = 0 as x on y gives b_yx*b_xy = (1/3)(7/2) = 7/6 > 1, which is impossible since that product is r^2; the admissible assignment is therefore x - 3y + 4 = 0 as x on y (b_xy = 3) and 2x - 7y + 8 = 0 as y on x (b_yx = 2/7), with r^2 = 6/7 <= 1. Hence b_xy + 7b_yx = 3 + 2 = 5; the inadmissible assignment would have given 35/6, which is not an option.

np = 4 and npq = 2 give q = 1/2, hence p = 1/2 and n = 8 (sympy returns this as the unique positive solution). P(X=1) = C(8,1)(1/2)(1/2)^7 = 8/256 = 1/32 by exact Fraction arithmetic, and the reconstructed distribution sums to 1 with mean 4 and variance 2 as a cross-check.
